fix_prompts.problem: Blade max drawdown 288.5% with Sharpe 0.057 — Norman FAIL verdict. Position sizing is structurally broken despite a real edge (PF 1.862, WR 56.8%).
fix_prompts.root_cause: Position sizing logic does not scale risk to session bankroll or enforce per-trade loss limits. The edge is real but the sizing is destroying it. Norman explicitly states: 'max drawdown of 288.5% is incompatible with long-term capital survival.' 226 trades, 48 sessions, net -$88.68 while the edge itself implies positive expectancy of $8.91/trade — the math only reconciles if oversized losses are wiping profits on losing trades.
fix_prompts.fix_prompt: Read the Blade agent source code — check /home/jase/jcf/blade/ or equivalent service directory. Locate the position sizing logic, specifically how lot size or contract size is calculated per trade. Do the following: (1) Identify whether there is any per-trade risk cap expressed as a percentage of session bankroll — if not, add one. Set max risk per trade to 1% of the session starting balance. (2) Identify whether there is a daily drawdown circuit breaker — if not, implement one. If session P&L drops below -5% of starting session balance, halt trading for the remainder of that session. (3) Identify whether stop losses are fixed-point or ATR-based — document which it is and verify the stop is being respected in execution. (4) Add a pre-trade check that calculates the dollar risk of the proposed trade (entry to stop loss × position size) and rejects any trade where dollar risk exceeds 1% of session bankroll. (5) Run a backtest or simulation against the existing 226-trade log to verify what the drawdown profile would have been under the new sizing rules. Compare projected max drawdown to the current 288.5% benchmark. Log the results. Verify the service restarts cleanly with: sudo systemctl restart blade (or equivalent). Confirm next session executes with new sizing parameters active.
fix_prompts.estimated_impact: Reducing per-trade risk to 1% of session bankroll with a -5% daily circuit breaker should compress max drawdown from 288.5% to under 30% based on the existing edge metrics, while preserving the $8.91/trade positive expectancy. This converts Blade from a capital-destruction risk to a viable production agent.

fix_prompts.problem: Kalshi settlement outcome tracking is non-existent. 24,598 log rows, last activity 2026-04-23, zero P&L accountability. Norman CRITICAL alert — unresolved for 46+ days.
fix_prompts.root_cause: The data pipeline records order placement events but does not capture settlement outcomes (win/loss/push, final P&L per contract). This is a logging architecture failure, not a strategy failure. Norman states: 'Settlement outcome tracking is non-existent — this is a systemic infrastructure failure.' Without settlement data, 408 historical trades and all future trades are analytically worthless.
fix_prompts.fix_prompt: Open the Kalshi bot source code — check /home/jase/jcf/kalshi-bot/ or the kalshi service directory. Do the following: (1) Review the existing log schema — identify what fields are currently captured per row (likely: timestamp, market_id, order_id, side, price, quantity, status). (2) Identify whether Kalshi's API provides settlement/resolution endpoints — check the Kalshi API docs for market resolution status, specifically GET /markets/{ticker} for 'result' field and GET /portfolio/positions or /portfolio/trades for settled P&L. (3) Write a settlement reconciliation function that: queries all open/filled positions from the last 90 days, checks each market's resolution status, records the outcome (YES_WIN / NO_WIN / VOID), calculates realized P&L per position (shares × (settlement_price - entry_price)), and writes results to a settlements table or appends a 'settlement_outcome' column to the existing log. (4) Schedule this reconciliation function to run daily at 08:00 UTC. (5) Backfill historical settlements where possible — attempt to resolve all 408 historical trades using the Kalshi API market history. (6) Add a monitoring alert: if any filled order has no settlement outcome after 48 hours past expected market close, log a WARNING. Verify the fix by running the reconciliation function manually and confirming at least one historical trade shows a settlement_outcome field populated. Check: sudo journalctl -u kalshi-bot -n 50 for any errors after restart.
fix_prompts.estimated_impact: Restoring settlement tracking unlocks P&L accountability for all future Kalshi trades and potentially recovers historical P&L data for up to 408 past trades. This unblocks Norman's ability to evaluate Kalshi's strategy and enables real capital allocation decisions on the bot.
